lessons: A one-session rise that undoes a one-session fall is read over both sessions before a cause is looked for: Genting 1.84 -> 1.80 -> 1.84 read 1.71 sigma on the second day alone.
A name with a significant negative drift reads an ordinary day as idiosyncratic strength: Genting's -0.25%/session drift at 2.1 standard errors makes a flat close count +0.25% as unexplained.

A blank index close may be filled a day later: the ^KLSE 10-08 close was blank until the 10:09Z fetch on 10-09, so a Bursa day decomposed before the next Bursa-hours fetch can be measured against the wrong bar.
